lessons.title: Arriving in a new country
lessons.goal: I can talk about arriving in a new country.

newItems.definition: A short stop between two flights on a trip.
newItems.example: We have a two-hour layover in Dubai.

newItems.definition: A small book of useful words in a foreign language.
newItems.example: She carries a phrasebook in her bag.

newItems.definition: To arrange and pay for a plane trip in advance.
newItems.example: We book a flight to Paris next month.

newItems.definition: To start a trip by car or on foot.
newItems.example: We hit the road early in the morning.

newItems.definition: To go from one country into another.
newItems.example: We cross the border by train.

mainWord.definition: A short stop between two flights on a trip.
mainWord.example: We have a two-hour layover in Dubai.

lessons.example: By the time we land, we will have flown for ten hours.
context: Daniel talks to Maya about his trip to Japan at work.
We book a flight to Paris next month. We hit the road at dawn.

Maya: When do you leave?
Daniel: We book a flight to Paris next month, and Japan is first on the list.
Maya: Do you have a long layover?
Daniel: Yes. We have a two-hour layover in Dubai. I carry my phrasebook in my bag.
Maya: Good. We hit the road at dawn, and then we cross the border by train.

lessons.title: Culture shock
lessons.goal: I can talk about culture shock.

newItems.definition: A confused feeling when everything around you is new.
newItems.example: Disorientation is common in the first week.

newItems.definition: Not known to you before; strange and new.
newItems.example: The food here is unfamiliar to me.

newItems.definition: To feel that you do not belong in a new place.
newItems.example: At first, he felt like a stranger in the new city.

newItems.definition: A problem when people cannot understand each other's language.
newItems.example: A language barrier makes simple shopping hard.

newItems.definition: A person who feels strange in a new place.
newItems.example: He felt like a fish out of water at first.

mainWord.definition: A confused feeling when everything around you is new.

lessons.title: Getting used to new customs

newItems.definition: The change from one place or way of life to another.

newItems.definition: To become part of a group without being noticed as different.
newItems.example: He tries to blend in with the local people.

newItems.definition: To become used to a new place and feel sure of yourself.

lessons.title: Homesickness and missing home

newItems.definition: The sad feeling of missing your home.
newItems.example: Homesickness is normal in the first month.

newItems.definition: To want to be back at home.
newItems.example: He misses home when the evenings are quiet.

newItems.definition: To feel that you do not belong in a place.

newItems.definition: A long distance away from the place where you live.

lessons.title: Making friends abroad

context: Daniel meets Sara at the airport and talks about travel.
Jet lag makes the first day very hard. Many immigrants work in this town.
dialogue: Daniel: Sara, do you know what an expatriate is?
Sara: Yes. An expatriate is a person who lives in a foreign country.
Daniel: What is a diaspora?
Sara: A diaspora is people from one country who live in many other countries.
Daniel: What about an outsider?
Sara: An outsider is a person who does not belong to a group. Jet lag makes the first day very hard.
